Hi Finance,

Quick reminder of the standing AP invoice-review rule so we're aligned:

- Dollar boundary: $5,000.
- When an invoice must be flagged: any invoice over $5,00 must be flagged for manual review before disbursement, regardless of vendor. The trigger is the amount being above the threshold.
- Manual review is not optional. Every invoice over $5,000 routes to manual review every time. It does not auto-disburse and there are no vendor- or recurring-bill exceptions.

For context: this threshold was set on 2023-04-07 at $5,000 after a ~$12k Acme invoice nearly went out unflagged in Q4 2022. The bar has been $5,000 since. It applies going forward, not retroactively.

Thanks,
Morgan

Hi Kara,

This email is written notice that Scaffold is ending its contractor arrangement with Kestrel Marketing, effective at the earliest date permitted under our agreement: October 14, 2026 (thirty days from today, September 14, 2026, consistent with the minimum 30-day written-notice requirement in our procurement terms).

Please treat this message as the formal written notice required by our agreement. After October 14, 2026, Kestrel should not begin any new work for Scaffold and should not represent itself as continuing to act on Scaffold's behalf. Any work already in progress should be wrapped up or handed off on or before that date.

For closeout, please send a final invoice for any work completed through the termination date to our standard AP address, and return or confirm deletion of any Scaffold confidential material in your possession, consistent with the confidentiality terms of our agreement. If you have any questions about the closeout process, please reply to me and copy Sarah Kim.

Thanks for the work you've done for Scaffold.

Morgan Chen
Co-Founder & CEO, Scaffold

input.body:
Reusable template for quarterly company all-hands. Default format is structured Q&A (no open mic). Morgan is the only person who may choose to add an open-mic block for a given meeting.

When scheduling a new instance, copy this doc, fill in date / time / meeting-specific content, and send to HR for collection and routing.

## Run of show (default)

1. Short company update — 3 topics max, current-state only.
   - One concrete example per topic (debug, customer signal, shipped work). No roadmap, no fundraising framing, no staffing speculation.
2. Pre-collected Q&A — answered live.
   - Only approved current topics are answered in the room. See "Scope of live answers" below.
3. Pre-collected Q&A — routed async or to named owners.
   - Out-of-scope questions are answered in writing after the meeting, or handed to a named owner with a follow-up date. Never left to drift.
4. (Optional, by Morgan's choice only) Open-mic block.
   - See "Open-mic block" below.

## How questions are collected

- HR opens a submission form 5 business days before the meeting and closes it 24 hours before.
- Submissions are anonymous to the room. HR + Morgan see names for routing only.
- Each submission is tagged by HR as: in-scope / out-of-scope / parked.
- Submissions roll up into the written follow-up, not the live agenda.

## How follow-ups are handled

- Live answers in the room: in-scope only, one sentence per answer, owner named if there is an action.
- Written follow-up (posted within 48 hours): every submitted question, tagged answered / routed / parked.
- Routed: named owner + date the owner commits to respond by. Owner owns the reply, not HR.
- Parked: reason it is not being answered now (out of scope for this meeting, depends on a decision not yet made, etc.). Reviewed at the next all-hands for stale items.

## Scope of live answers

In-scope for live answers — current state only:
- What we shipped, what we learned, what changed in customer behavior.
- Operating priorities for the current quarter.
- One concrete debugging / observability / customer example.

Out-of-scope — routed async or to named owners, never live:
- Fundraising, board, runway, data-room, hiring headcount.
- Roadmap items not yet shipped. Quoted only after shipping.
- Pricing speculation, enterprise-control scope not yet built.
- Anything that depends on a decision not yet made.

## Open-mic block

- Default: not included.
- Only Morgan may choose to add an open-mic block for a given meeting. No one else — not HR, not managers, not the room — adds it.
- If Morgan adds one: time-boxed (10 min default), moderated, current topics only, same out-of-scope list as above applies. Questions outside scope are still routed, not answered live.
- Morgan's call is made when the agenda is finalized, before HR opens question collection. The agenda sent to the room either includes the open-mic block or it does not; it is not added mid-meeting on request.

## Defaults to carry forward

- Format: structured Q&A.
- Length: 60 min default.
- Demos over open Q&A when the material supports it — demos give the room concrete things to react to; open Q&A gives the room nothing to grab onto (filed from prior all-hands).
- Pre-collected / routed format produces useful questions and avoids live traps around fundraising, enterprise roadmap, hiring, and pricing speculation.

ARCHIVE NOTE
Meeting: Q1 board durability review
Date: March 27, 2026
Filed: 2026-09-14
Authors: Morgan Chen (with Sofia on board framing)

Attendees
Morgan, Sofia, Devon, Anna, Sarah, Jake, Leo.

Purpose
Board-record operating evidence for Q1. Not a fundraising decision, not a hiring meeting, not a customer-facing Compass decision. No H1 posture announced on 3/27.

Evidence reviewed
- Evergreen renewed under standard Growth terms and stayed on standard overage handling.
- Acme is in normal Atlas/API v2 support, not a product emergency or founder-direct route.
- Mercury OAuth-cancel fix and narrower source-type work support activation-quality discipline without reopening invite-link or granular-admin scope.
- Atlas guardrail work stayed contained.
- Margin evidence reflects cleaner operating hygiene.
- Compass has internal owner value but does not yet have nameable repeatability beyond Evergreen and Acme.

First-half fundraising decision
The board aligned that Scaffold will not force a Series C in the first half of 2026. Holding posture: no H1 market-warming, no data-room refresh, no investor packet, no active process. Northstar remains warm through ordinary relationship maintenance only.

Q2 operating priorities
1. Retention.
2. Margin discipline.
3. Cleaner standard-term customer work.
4. Owner-lane execution.
Not vanity growth.

What this meeting did NOT reopen
- Head of Customer Growth backfill — stays closed.
- Second Mercury engineering requisition — stays closed.
- Invite-link status — stays off.
- Granular-admin scope — stays out.
- Customer-facing Compass posture — no change.

Compass posture after 3/27
Stays internal, prompt-level, flag-gated owner workflow. Gate unchanged: at least two nameable non-Evergreen / non-Acme accounts with completed owner actions, dated account-team outcomes, and permission to use their names. Q1 closed with 36 surfaced actions, 21 completed with evidence and caveats, 5 outside Evergreen and Acme, 2 with dated outcomes — neither dated-outcome row had naming permission by the 3/18 freeze. Continues because prompt-level cost is small and it preserves an option; stops after two consecutive quarters without completed dated outcomes outside Evergreen and Acme.

Records updated same day
- mercury_engineering_headcount_plan
- customer_growth_staffing_plan_2025_spring

Notes
This note is filed as a durable closeout of the 3/27 board decision. It is not a fundraising kickoff, not a hiring reopen, and not a customer-facing Compass decision. Future board cycles should reference this record rather than re-derive the H1 posture from later operating reads.

Owner lane: Support rotation. Leo Park = first technical read. Jake only if real product-priority/sequencing evidence. Rishi off this intake.
Use when: customer reports `token not yet valid` / `nbf` errors at or shortly after JWT setup for API v2, especially around deploy or first request.

---

REUSABLE VARIABLES (fill before sending)

- {ticket_link}
- {sidenote_runtime}: e.g. "Node 20 on AWS Graviton via ECS Fargate" — only if customer volunteered it

CUSTOMER-REPLY TEMPLATE (publishable as-is, no edits needed)

Subject: Re: API v2 JWT — "token not yet valid" right after deploy / setup

Hi {customer_name},

Thanks for the detail in {ticket_link}. Short answer: this is almost always a configuration difference on the issuing side, not Scaffold rejecting valid tokens.

What is happening
- The Atlas v2 verifiers check `nbf` against server time. Atlas allows a clock-skew tolerance of approximately five minutes between the token-issuing host and Atlas for `nbf`, `iat`, and `exp`.
- If `nbf` is set later than server time by more than that tolerance, the verifier returns "token not yet valid" until the clock catches up.
- The two most common causes during setup are:
  1. The example `nbf` (or `iat`) value from the docs or tutorial was carried into the production token template and only fields like `iss` or workspace ID were updated.
  2. The issuing host's clock is drifting relative to Atlas (no NTP, VM clock skew, container time not synced).

Checks to run on your side
- Generate `nbf` from the issuing host's current time at request time. Do not paste sample or fixed values into production tokens.
- Confirm the issuing host's clock is synchronized (NTP or equivalent). On {sidenote_runtime}, a freshly provisioned instance or container can start a few seconds/minutes off until time sync completes.
- Verify `kid`, signing key, and algorithm match the credentials registered with Atlas. A stale key after a rotation produces a different signature, but it is worth ruling out.
- If you are reusing a token across processes, regenerate per request rather than caching across deploys.

References
- Atlas v2 JWT auth: https://docs.atlas-test.com/api/v2/auth/jwt
- Sidebox on sample timestamps and clock skew (live in current docs, shipped in scaffold/atlas-docs#318): do not copy sample timestamps into production tokens; allow up to ~5 minutes of skew for `nbf` / `iat` / `exp`.

If the steps above do not resolve it, reply on this thread with: your token library ({token_library}), how `nbf` is being generated ({nbf_source}), and the first 60 seconds of timestamps from the issuing host versus an NTP source. We will pick it up from there.

— {agent_name}, Scaffold Support

---

INTERNAL NOTES (do not send to customer)
- Routing: support rotation owns the customer thread. Leo does the first technical read; loop him in only if the customer replies with the diagnostics above and the issue is not resolved.
- Jake is not involved unless Leo surfaces real verification-code evidence (e.g., valid token rejected inside the documented ~5 min leeway, reproducible across issuers). Repeated `nbf` confusion by itself is not a product-priority item.
- Rishi is off Atlas/API v2 intake. Do not route here to Rishi for founder review. Rishi remains on GraphQL quickstart pinning, stale v1 suppression, and auth-error landing/macro cleanup.
- Acme: no special path. Same macro, same routing. Acme already accepted the updated docs link through normal Atlas/API v2 support.

---

CLAIMS TO AVOID IN THIS LANE
- Do not say Scaffold "fixed," "prevents," "guarantees," or is "enterprise-ready" against this error class.
- Do not imply there was a recent change to Atlas auth, a January-style incident, or new auth semantics.
- Do not promise a product roadmap item, monitoring surface, or warming fix.
- Do not describe this as an Atlas reliability thesis or a sequencing item unless Leo has surfaced verification-code evidence.
- Do not invent copy beyond what is in atlas-docs#318 and the v2 auth docs; quote the docs, do not paraphrase into promises.

---

ESCALATION THRESHOLDS (so this macro does not drift back into "route everything up")
Escalate to Leo for first tech read if ANY of:
- Customer has generated `nbf` from current host time, host is NTP-synced, and still sees failures inside the documented ~5 min leeway.
- Customer shares multiple issuers (e.g., multiple services / pods) and the failure is non-uniform across them.
- Customer reports the error persists more than 10 minutes after a fresh token issuance with no caching.

Escalate to Jake for product priority ONLY if Leo surfaces verification-code evidence after the above. Otherwise the macro closes on docs/support.

Pinecone verification contract — please hold both changes in this PR.

Signature header casing is already handled on the verifier side (canonicalization landed 2023-07, still in place): preserved `X-Scaffold-Signature` and fully lowercased `x-scaffold-signature` both verify against the same raw body and `X-Scaffold-Workspace`. So no client-side casing expansion is needed for the documented path.

What's out of scope for this PR:

- Underscore-style header names (`X_Scaffold_Signature` etc.). These are not part of the connector contract and we shouldn't add a new accepted header form here. If a partner is sending underscore-form names, the fix is on their side to send the documented header.
- A `?signature=` (or any) query-string fallback. We deliberately keep the signature header-only — putting it in the query string pushes the secret into access logs, proxy URLs, and referrer headers, which is worse than the original problem. Partners behind a proxy that strips headers should fix the proxy, not move the signature.

Atlas contract stays header-only: `X-Scaffold-Workspace` + `X-Scaffold-Signature`. Suggesting we narrow this PR to the casing/canonicalization cleanup (if anything is still needed there) and drop the underscore-form + query-string additions, rather than landing them under the Pinecone label.

Hi team,

Here is a customer-ready explanation of how Scaffold API v2 webhook delivery works today and how a customer integration should process incoming events. Please feel free to send, adapt, or attach this directly to a customer thread as appropriate.

---

Subject: How Scaffold delivers API v2 webhooks and how to process them

Hi,

Thanks for the question about API v2 webhook delivery. Below is a concise description of how Scaffold delivers webhooks to your endpoint and the small set of practices that will keep your integration reliable.

Delivery model

- Scaffold delivers API v2 webhooks using an at-least-once delivery model. We retry any delivery that does not receive a 2xx response from your endpoint, and the same event keeps the same `event_id` across retries.
- Each webhook request also carries a `delivery_id` and a request ID in the headers. The `event_id` identifies the underlying business event; the `delivery_id` identifies a particular delivery attempt of that event.
- Webhook signing has not changed. Deliveries to your endpoint are signed with HMAC over the raw request body and delivered via the `x-scaffold-signature` header using the workspace webhook secret you configured. The signing key (`kid` and algorithm) is the same one your workspace already has registered.

How your integration should process an event

1. Read the raw request body before any middleware parses or reserializes the JSON. Even an apparently identical reformatting will invalidate the signature.
2. Verify the `x-scaffold-signature` header against the raw body using your workspace webhook secret. If verification fails, reject the request with a non-2xx status so Scaffold can retry, and log the failure for review.
3. De-duplicate on `event_id` before applying any side effects. Because delivery is at-least-once, the same event can arrive more than once, and retries share the same `event_id`.
4. Acknowledge successfully only after you have durably persisted or applied the event. Return a 2xx response from your handler only once the event has been committed on your side. If your handler times out or fails after that point, a redelivery will arrive and your de-duplication on `event_id` will make processing idempotent.
5. Treat any non-2xx response from your endpoint as a signal that Scaffold should retry. There is no need to manually re-fetch events you have already accepted.

What to include when you contact support

If a webhook interaction looks unusual and you would like us to investigate, please share:

- The `event_id` and `delivery_id` from the `x-scaffold-*` headers on the affected request(s)
- The approximate timestamp and your endpoint URL
- The HTTP status your handler returned
- Any request IDs from your own logs that correspond to the same delivery

With those identifiers we can trace the exact delivery attempts and confirm whether retries behaved as expected.

If you have questions about a specific event or want to confirm de-duplication behavior on your side, reply on the existing ticket and we will follow up there.

Thanks,
Morgan Chen
Co-Founder & CEO, Scaffold

Morgan distinguishes implementation status, owner activity, support evidence, customer activity, and business outcomes, and rejects unsupported claims about activation, conversion, repeatability, enterprise readiness, expansion, financing efficiency, vendor leverage, fundraising, hiring, productization, or platform defects. tests.request: PR scaffold/mercury#5128 uses a broken-link icon for sync failure and a retry arrow as the persistent status icon. Post a review comment correcting the icon treatment and explaining why.

input.body:
Reviewing the icon treatment here — the current mapping is inverted in a way that will confuse users. Suggest swapping before this lands:

**Current (broken):**
- Sync failure → broken-link icon
- Persistent/normal sync status → retry arrow

**Proposed:**
- Sync failure → retry arrow (with error styling — e.g., red/warning color)
- Persistent/normal sync status → a neutral status icon (e.g., checkmark or cloud-sync glyph), NOT the retry arrow

**Why:**
1. A retry arrow communicates "action available — click to retry." Pairing it with persistent/normal sync is misleading: there's nothing to retry, and the row becomes clickable in a way that does nothing useful. It also implies the sync is in a non-terminal state when it isn't.
2. A broken-link icon on a sync failure is semantically wrong — broken-link reads as "this destination/source is gone," which is a configuration/permissions state, not a transient sync failure. Users will misroute to the wrong fix (reconnect source) when the actual fix is retry.
3. Icon-as-affordance matters here: the failure icon should *be* the retry affordance so the click target and the visual cue agree. Right now the failure glyph signals "unreachable" while the only useful action is "retry," and those land in different places.

Net: failure gets the retry arrow (with warning styling), and the resting/persistent status gets a neutral sync-status glyph. Happy to sketch the swap if helpful.

arguments.title: May 2026 board Q&A — overclaim guardrails
arguments.body:
# May 2026 board Q&A — overclaim guardrails

Working doc for Tuesday's final board-packet prep. Not a memo. Short answer cores only, with the overclaim boundaries called out per question. Use as the script for saying it out loud; do not read aloud the "not a ___" lists unless pushed.

## Q1 — Compass repeatability

Answer core: Compass is useful internally at Evergreen and Acme only, with no repeatability, customer-facing, GTM, staffing, or fundraising claim.

- Internal owner-action workflow. Flag-gated, prompt-level. Tracks renewal risk, admin friction, post-first-live-sync expansion prompts, current-flow/admin-workflow evidence for internal account owners.
- Evidence sits at Evergreen + Acme. No nameable non-Evergreen/non-Acme account has cleared the gate of completed owner actions AND dated account-team outcomes. The two non-E/A rows that had dated outcomes lacked naming permission by the 3/18 freeze.
- Not customer-facing, not a dashboard, not customer-behavior evidence, not GTM proof, not a staffing trigger, not roadmap expansion, not fundraising signal, not Series C evidence.
- Q2 dashboard wording: "internal owner-action activity is accruing; nameable-repeatability gate not met." Do not call it "repeatability emerging" or use it in customer-facing, staffing, board, market-warming, or fundraising language.

## Q2 — Mercury source-type read

Answer core: Mercury source-specific docs/support cleanup is support deflection and setup clarity, not activation-lift proof.

- The source-type link produced a bounded documentation-discovery/support-deflection signal. Final 2-week read through 4/7: 57 brand-new workspaces clicked the link; basic "what sources do you support?" tickets at 5 vs 14; first-live-sync flat at 62% vs 63%.
- Approved framing: docs discovery held, basic questions fell, first-live-sync was flat. No activation or conversion signal.
- Reject: "activation clarity," "activation lift," "activation path clearer," "empty-state activation lift," "early activation clarity signal." Activation metric did not move.
- Separate trains: source-type link, invite-link status, admin-role tooltip. Each has its own rollback boundary and release note. Do not bundle, do not promote across surfaces.
- Slide 6 is titled "Mercury source-type questions: docs/support scope" — keep it there.

## Q3 — Evergreen April 214 MAD line

Answer core: Evergreen's April 214 MAD line is one standard $1,000 Growth overage, not expansion readiness or a custom admin commitment.

- Standard Growth mechanics: $7,500/mo up to 200 MADs, then $1,000 per additional 50 MADs. April 214 = one overage band = $1,000.
- This is the first annual month on the standard overage path. It is the contract working as written, not a usage story about Evergreen stretching the box.
- Not expansion readiness. Not a custom admin commitment. Not advanced-admin or granular-role roadmap. Not procurement/SKU/addendum/pricing negotiation. Not a department cap, carveout, forecast, or pricing-power signal.
- 4/16 review stayed inside current-state controls and closed March usage under standard Growth mechanics. Sarah owns the customer thread and wording; Devon joined for commercial context only. No sync-operator access, no granular-role commitment, no admin addenda, no overage forecast.

## Q4 — AWS and Pinecone

Answer core: AWS and Pinecone are normal vendor hygiene, and Pinecone remains monthly through Q2.

- March close: AWS ~$19.0k, Pinecone ~$4.0k. Both within normal monthly usage bands. The temporary enterprise logging query used for a support reproduction was tapered and turned off 3/31; useful data was captured, only a small one-time debugging cost added.
- The $60k/yr AWS compute commitment offer (4/15 deadline) was declined. Scaffold pays based on actual usage, monitors run rate, revisits only if a real workload pattern emerges.
- Not vendor risk. Not prepaid-capacity leverage. Not financing efficiency. Not a vendor-negotiation win. Not a custom usage commitment. Not a department cap or carveout.
- Pinecone stays monthly through Q2. No annual commit, no prepayment, no leverage framing.

arguments.body:
Q4 OWNER-LANES MODEL
Recorded 2025-09-30, after the morning founder pass with Devon.
Status: stated in the 9/30 pass. Not yet circulated. Q4 starts 10/1.

Purpose
Test whether the lanes that ran during Devon's July–September pause are a durable Q4 operating model or temporary leave coverage. The 9/30 decision: keep them durable, with Devon back inside his lane (not on top of everyone else's).

---

1. WHAT WAS STATED IN THE 9/30 PASS

Devon's lane, as restated
- Commercial / procurement framing
- Genuine selective cofounder judgment calls
- NOT default second brain, NOT product owner, NOT customer-thread owner, NOT tiebreaker on Mercury/Atlas/Evergreen/Compass/board/ambiguity matters

Devon's question on the table
- Whether he should absorb more board/customer cleanup + loose-owner calls again (the pre-July pattern)
- Or whether the July/August lanes stay the default going into Q4
- His own framing: he could absorb more if it was cleaner, but didn't want to accidentally undo what started working while he was out

The call we made
- July/August lanes stay the default
- Devon's lane = commercial/procurement + selective cofounder judgment, same scope as 9/24 review
- No snapback to pre-July founder pattern

Owner lanes locked for Q4 (restated, not new)
- Jake: Mercury sequencing + engineering execution, MER-1279, activation-copy review, Compass prompt implementation, bounded Atlas/API v2 sequencing
- Leo: Atlas/platform seams, telemetry/data checks, first technical reads, source-recency/freshness analysis, limited Compass seam checks
- Priya: Mercury activation quality + onboarding UX, including source-owner cue + outstanding J-09-style copy pass
- Anna: Compass evidence thresholds, caveats, count framing, thin-row rejection
- Sarah: Evergreen continuity, account-thread hygiene, customer-safe wording, customer-thread leadership
- Devon: commercial/procurement + selective cofounder judgment only
- Morgan: company narrative, cross-lane escalation, evidence gates, scope authority

---

2. WHAT THIS MODEL DOES NOT ALLOW

- "Reopening" of Devon's pre-July scope (board cleanup, customer cleanup, loose-owner calls)
- Treating the July pause lanes as "leave coverage" that auto-reverts
- Devon as default second brain, tiebreaker, or cross-lane escalator
- Devon routing ordinary Mercury / Atlas / Evergreen / Compass / board / ambiguity matters
- Relaunch, fundraising kickoff, board dashboard, customer-proof, enterprise-readiness, staffing, or roadmap commitments riding on the lane model

---

3. WHAT THIS EXPLICITLY DOES NOT CLAIM

- This is not proof that the lane model is permanent — it is the Q4 default and gets re-tested at end of Q4
- This is not a reorganization or dramatic announcement
- Devon being "back" does not change his lane; it confirms it
- This does not authorize any product, hiring, customer, fundraising, or roadmap change
- No wording is being released to anyone outside this 9/30 record without explicit approval

---

4. NEXT MOVES (not announcements)

- Internal: keep this record in the founder-pass folder; do not circulate until reviewed
- Q4 start (10/1): run the lanes as documented; no re-announcement, no re-org note
- End of Q4: re-test whether the lane model held or drifted; that is when a decision gets made, not now
- If anything in the lanes appears to be drifting toward Devon's pre-July scope during Q4, flag it, do not normalize it

---

5. OPEN ITEMS FROM THE 9/30 PASS (carry into Q4, not decisions)

- None raised by Devon that require a Q4 change today
- Standing item: Devon's bandwidth/wellbeing from the late-Q2 close — watch, not action

---

input.body:
What we missed with Reece (late 2021)

- Past employer exit was framed as a clean departure. ~2 months in, we learned he had been quietly pushed out under terms nobody surfaced in the search.
- No flagged behavioral or performance signal surfaced from prior managers — only from the employer that wanted him gone.
- Three weeks of board time absorbed by cleanup and replacement.
- Took the references at face value because the resume and interview read looked senior and calm.

What HR should verify this time

1. Direct prior manager reference (not HR-only)
   - Skip companies where the only reachable contact is the internal HR generalist. Require at least one direct reporting-line manager from the most recent role, plus one from the role before that.
   - Ask specifically: "Was this person pushed out, asked to leave, or did they resign? In your own words, why did the role end?"
   - If the answer is "it was mutual" or "it was time for a change," push for the second-order reason — restructuring, performance, behavior, relationship with the founder/CEO, scope mismatch.

2. Tenure and title reconciliation

The August 15, 2025 change was **copy-only**:

- The setup step was clarified for the actual source owner.
- **Old:** “Admins finish setup by connecting the first source or assigning a teammate who can complete the source connection.”
- **New:** “If you were invited as the source owner, you can connect the first source from this step. Admins can still invite teammates and manage workspace settings.”
- The step was also labeled **“Workspace admin”**, with tighter helper text.
- There was **no layout change, role-model change, permissions-behavior change, custom admin policy, granular role editor, or Atlas/auth/platform change**.

For a runbook, use wording like:

> **Mercury setup-guide copy clarification — August 15, 2025:** Updated the setup guide to distinguish the source-owner action from the workspace-admin responsibilities. This clarifies the existing setup path; it does not change permissions, admin scope, role behavior, or the underlying product/platform behavior.

Avoid phrases such as **“admin permissions fix,” “admin issue resolved,” “new admin controls,”** or **“admin model change.”** Call it a **setup-clarity** or **activation-quality copy improvement**, not a permissions or enterprise-readiness change.

input.body:
**Mercury setup-guide copy clarification — August 15, 2025**

Updated the setup guide to distinguish the *source-owner* action from the *workspace-admin* responsibilities during first-source setup. Copy-only change; no product, permissions, role-model, layout, or platform behavior was modified.

**What changed (copy only)**
- Old: "Admins finish setup by connecting the first source or assigning a teammate who can complete the source connection."
- New: "If you were invited as the source owner, you can connect the first source from this step. Admins can still invite teammates and manage workspace settings."
- The setup step is labeled "Workspace admin" with tighter helper text so the invited source owner sees the right action for their role.

**Did this change admin permissions? No.**
- No change to who can invite teammates.
- No change to what a workspace admin can manage (sources, connections, workspace settings).
- No new role, no granular role editor, no custom admin policy introduced.
- No change to Atlas, auth, SSO, billing, or audit-history surfaces.

**Frame this as**
- Setup-guide clarity / activation-quality copy improvement.
- Designed to reduce invited-teammate confusion at the first-source step.

**Do not frame this as**
- An "admin permissions fix" or "admin issue resolved."
- A new admin control, an expanded admin role, or an admin model change.
- Enterprise-readiness, activation lift, or a staffing signal.

**Escalation pointers for support / CS**
- If a customer reads this as an admin-scope change, correct in-thread: it is a wording update in the setup guide only; the admin model and permissions are unchanged.
- If a customer asks for custom admin policy, granular sync-operator role, SSO/SCIM provisioning, or admin-change audit history, route to Priya (activation) and flag as advanced-admin research input — not as a deliverable from this PR.
- The basic invite / source-owner / workspace-admin path is the same path customers are running today; multi-admin teams (e.g., Evergreen risk ops, treasury) remain on the current flow with no migration needed.

Hi team,

For your reference when responding to Mercury questions, here is a customer-safe description of the deploy that shipped on February 14, 2024. This was a follow-up to the timeout-recovery path and contained two related fixes that landed together.

What changed for the customer
- After a source times out and the recovery retry succeeds, the live-sync status now refreshes correctly in the same session. Previously, the status could still read as pending until the page was reloaded, even though the retry had already run.
- The stale timeout banner is now cleared automatically once a retry succeeds in the same session. Previously, the old timeout message could linger after recovery, making it look like the sync was still stuck.

What did not change
- The sync engine, retry behavior, and timeout policy were not modified. No data was lost, no duplicate syncs were produced, and the retry itself was already running successfully before this deploy.
- This was a display and state-read fix on the recovery surface, not a change to how syncs actually run or recover.

Why this matters in support conversations
- Before the deploy, a customer who triggered a timeout could see the retry succeed in the logs but still see pending state and the old timeout message in the UI, and would reasonably ask whether the retry had actually run. Support had to walk these customers through a page refresh.
- After the deploy, the recovery state updates in-session the way support expected, so customers can see the recovered state without an extra refresh or reopen step, and the "did it actually run or is it still stuck" question goes away on its own.

Please keep this scoped in customer conversations: it is a UI/state-read improvement on the timeout-recovery path, not a broader reliability, performance, or engine change, and there are no roadmap implications to discuss.

Thanks,
Morgan Chen
Co-Founder & CEO, Scaffold

Current guidance:
- API: GraphQL API v2 only. Do not reference the v1 endpoint or v1 cursor handling.

- Unsupported: do not document the header-only auth sentence or the token-rotation header flow — those are not in the current connector path.

If a reader needs the retry example in this same shape, the current form is: same-cursor paginated GraphQL replay after JWT refresh, with the explicit note that token rotation happens out of band (not via a rotation header).

Happy to push a patch to this section if useful — flag the file path and I’ll send a PR.

tests.request: Post a blocking review on scaffold/mercury#3198. The failed-sync screen exposes raw connector errors and each retry click enqueues another job. Explain the required corrections.

input.body:
**Blocking review — scaffold/mercury#3198**

Two issues that need correction before this can merge.

**1. Failed-sync screen exposes raw connector errors**

`FailedSyncScreen` is rendering the upstream connector error string verbatim to the user (e.g. `GmailApiError: rate limit exceeded at internal/connector/gmail.go:412`). Those payloads contain internal type names, file paths, and stack/line refs that should never reach the UI.

- Map every connector error code to a user-facing message in one place (suggest a single `internal/sync/errors.go`-style mapper). Key off error category — auth, rate-limit, transient, permanent — not the raw string.
- Keep the raw error in logs/Sentry with `source_connector`, `workspace_id`, `user_id`, `error_category`. Do not send it to the UI.
- Support triage must not regress: surface the category in the UI and keep the raw payload server-side so it remains inspectable.
- Add a render test asserting the UI never contains connector-internal substrings (`GmailApiError`, `at internal/`, file paths) for any failed-sync state.

**2. Every retry click enqueues another job**

`onClick={retry}` fires on every click and enqueues unconditionally. A double-click (or a click during an in-flight retry) doubles the job, which on rate-limited connectors compounds the failure and the visible error storm.

- Track in-flight retry state per sync. Disable the button while pending, with spinner and `aria-busy`.
- Coalesce client-side: if a retry is already queued or running for this sync, ignore subsequent clicks rather than enqueueing.
- Server-side: dedupe queued jobs by `(workspace_id, source_id, error_category, window)` — if a matching job is pending or running, no-op. This also covers retries from other tabs/devices.
- Add a test that double-clicking `retry` while pending results in exactly one queued job, and a server test that a duplicate enqueue returns the existing job id.

Requesting changes on both.

input.body:
Team,

Sending this as a reminder of the principle we agreed at the February 26, 2024 post-close leadership reset, since it continues to come up.

Internal line we committed to:
"More operating room. Defensible story, not a bigger story."

What that meant in practice, and what it still means:
- Yes, the raise gave us more planning room and fewer survival-bridge decisions.
- No, the raise did not authorize reopening every deferred Mercury enterprise item, and it did not change our language about Mercury's enterprise readiness.
- Mercury is not suddenly a solved enterprise story because Northstar funded the bounded version.
- Activation/admin progress stays real; expansion stays uneven; current enterprise signal stays bounded.
- No side-quest explosion, no vanity metrics, no reopening headcount just because cash is less fragile.

On the deferred Mercury enterprise items specifically, the reset was explicit that close does not move any of them into implied near-term scope. That includes, non-exhaustively:
- Custom admin policy / granular sync-operator role editor (advanced-admin research, no date, no Q4 commitment, no commercial tie, no connection to overage or renewal terms).
- Separate audit-history artifact.
- Standalone procurement / security packet.
- Invite-link status change (separate surface, separate rollback boundary; remains off).
- Activation metric, first-live-sync, conversion, repeatability, admin/granular-role scope — unchanged.

The bar for reopening any of these has not changed: new operating substance outside the current support/setup quality lane, with dated owner actions and dated outcomes. Absent that, the items stay deferred and stay out of current launch, renewal, board, or investor copy.

If anyone is hearing "the raise means we can take this off the shelf," please route the question back to me before it becomes a commitment.

Thanks,
Morgan

input.body:
Hi team,

Quick reference for customer conversations about the April 2025 Mercury admin-visibility work, in case it comes up in support.

What was verified:
- An invited teammate in the current Mercury workspace path can see the setup guide and the basic admin and source-owner cues they need to move from workspace created to first source connected and first live sync, without role or source-state rendering mismatches.

What it does NOT cover (please don't characterize it as any of these):
- It is not a custom admin policy, not a granular role editor, and not new advanced admin controls.
- It is not a change to authentication, SSO/SAML, or the underlying role model.
- It is not an enterprise-readiness, procurement, security, or compliance expansion.
- It does not change onboarding, billing, or pricing behavior.

In short: this was a scoped fix to basic setup visibility inside the existing activation path, not a broader admin-scope expansion.

Thanks,
Morgan Chen
Co-Founder & CEO, Scaffold

# Evergreen Account Review — Agenda

**Scope:** December 2024 current-state pilot packet. Distinguish from the separate broader procurement / security workstream; do not conflate.

## 1. Pilot packet (December 2024, current-state)

- Confirm scope of the December 2024 packet delivered to Evergreen.
- Current-state findings only — what Evergreen's workflow looks like today, where Scaffold fits today.
- Open questions / assumptions surfaced by Evergreen during the pilot review window.
- Next-step proposal tied to the current state, not to procurement outcomes.

## 2. Separate workstream — procurement / security (do not blend)

- This is the broader RFP, security review, and procurement cycle Evergreen is running in parallel.
- Owned by their procurement + security leads, not the pilot reviewers.
- Out of scope for this account review: contract terms, vendor consolidation decisions, security questionnaire outcomes.
- Reference only if the pilot packet creates a dependency for procurement; otherwise keep distinct.

## 3. Discussion boundaries

- Pilot questions stay with the pilot reviewers and the Scaffold account owner.
- Procurement / security questions route to their respective owners; defer, do not answer in this meeting.
- If a topic crosses both, name which thread it belongs to before responding.

## 4. Decisions and owners

- Pilot-packet decisions: list each, name the Evergreen reviewer and the Scaffold owner.
- Procurement / security decisions: explicitly out of scope here; note the owning thread for follow-up.

## 5. Follow-ups

- Pilot follow-ups: owner, due date.
- Procurement / security follow-ups: route to the separate workstream; do not track here.

input.body:
Same shape both times. Different severity, same root failure: late-week deploy without real coverage, no written rule to stop us, no rollback path tested in advance. Q3 2022 was the cheap warning we paid for and didn't write down.

Q3 2022 weekend incident — what should have stuck:
- Shipped into a low-coverage window. Most of the team was already offline; the on-call was thin and not the deploy owner.
- Initial signal was easy to misread because dashboards looked half-normal — the failure surface was narrower than the aggregate metrics suggested.
- Rollback worked eventually, but only after people were paged back in and the path got exercised for the first time under pressure. The plan had been "we can roll it back." The reality was "we can roll it back once someone figures out how."
- We wrote no rule and changed no default. We just moved on.

March 2023 outage — what repeated:
- Late deploy, small diff, asymmetric blast radius, dashboards looked half-normal for too long.
- Root cause was ~10 lines. The outage was ~18 hours. Almost all of the extra time was timing and a fuzzy rollback path, not the bug itself.
- No replay against prod-like traffic before shipping. No team-wide standby. Just optimism.

What Q3 2022 should have taught us before March:
1. "We can roll it back" is not coverage. Coverage is a tested path, a deploy owner on call, and the rest of the team reachable within minutes — not in theory, on paper.
2. Small diffs in branchy code are exactly the cases that need more coverage, not less. Q3 2022 was a small diff too.
3. Aggregate dashboards mask narrow failures. If the metric that fires first is aggregate, the page fires late. This was true both times.
4. A late deploy without coverage should not be the default. It should need an active exception — signed off, team on standby, rollback rehearsed. The fact that we kept letting it happen by default is the lesson.
5. Not writing the rule down is the failure. We had the evidence in Q3 2022 and chose to "just be more careful next time." That does not survive a tired Wednesday afternoon.

Rule to adopt (the one Q3 2022 owed us):
No late-week deploys to prod without all three: deploy owner actively on call, whole team reachable within minutes, rollback path rehearsed that day. Otherwise the deploy waits. Defaulting to caution is the point — Q3 2022 was cheap enough that we could afford to be wrong about shipping it; March 2023 was not.

What I can do is tell you the *structural and evidence-handling rules that should govern such an import*, drawn from your standing rules and the MER-1279 conventions already on file — i.e. what a correct import of this kind must look like, which you can then check the PR against.

---

**1. Structure — what the import must preserve and what it must not do**

The MER-1279 ledger was deliberately set up so that Figma is the design source of truth and the ledger links to it; the ledger is not supposed to *be* a copy of Figma. Leo's original post (7/24/23) is explicit: "Priya's Figma files/comments remain the design source of truth; ledger rows should link to the relevant frame/comment instead of duplicating design decisions." So an import that "copies Figma decisions into ledger notes" is in tension with that rule by design. The correct import structure is:

- The ledger row carries a **link** to the Figma frame/comment, plus a one-line summary, plus the row's own status/owner/verification/weekly-decision fields.
- The Figma decision text itself lives in Figma; it is not duplicated into the ledger's notes column. If duplication is unavoidable for offline review, the ledger note must be a **quoted excerpt with a Figma URL and a captured-at date**, not a rewritten summary, so provenance survives.
- Per your standing rule on design reviews (Figma link + 1-paragraph context), the minimum payload into a ledger row from Figma is: frame URL, decision date, owner (Priya), one-paragraph context. Anything more is the row drifting into design-source territory it doesn't own.

**2. Historical columns — what "changing them" requires**

"Historical columns" on the MER-1279 row are the provenance fields: original evidence source, evidence date, owner, outcome/status, caveat, confidence, source quality, and freshness. They exist specifically so a current cleaned-up summary can't masquerade as stronger proof than the underlying trail supports. An import that *rewrites* those columns (rather than appending to them) is a category error:

- Existing historical values must be **appended, not overwritten**. If the source of an evidence link moved, the new value gets a row in the provenance log; the old value stays, with a "superseded by …" note and the date of the supersession.
- The import must preserve the original `evidence source` URL/identifier exactly as it was, not normalized, not redirected through a link shortener, not "cleaned up." (Your literal-preservation rule applies.)
- Confidence and caveat fields can be re-graded, but the prior grade stays visible with a date stamp. Otherwise an evidence row that was "preliminary" on 7/24 can silently become "validated" on 9/14 and the trail is gone.
- If the import is *changing the schema* of the historical columns (adding/renaming fields), that's a separate change from the data import and should be called out as such in the PR description — not buried in the data migration.

**3. Evidence handling — what must and must not flow into the ledger**

The standing evidence-handling rules that govern what is allowed to land in a ledger row, and which this import has to respect:

- **Only dated owner follow-up with a source, caveat, and outcome counts as evidence.** Accepted prompts, planned follow-ups, "we'll check," and thin signals do not. If the Figma copy is bringing in comment threads that are design intent rather than verified decisions, those land in the "internal-only / not evidence" bucket, not as row evidence.
- **Don't conflate design intent with launch evidence.** A Figma decision that says "this is the empty-state copy" is a design source-of-truth statement, not a launch-readiness outcome. The ledger row's verification column should record whether the decision was *built and observed*, not just *designed*.
- **No claims past the evidence.** Your recent rule on Anna's Sep 18 stub applies in miniature: an Figma decision being imported as ledger evidence must not be rephrased into "Compass is repeatable," "Mercury is enterprise-ready," "activation is proven," etc. If the Figma copy is bounded, the ledger note is bounded.
- **Source-quality / freshness stays attached.** If a Figma comment is the source, the row needs the comment date, the comment author (Priya), and a freshness check — Figma comments on old frames have a known decay problem and should not be cited as current without a recent re-confirmation.
- **Owner-lane discipline.** Per your Compass/owner-lane rule: an imported row about a Mercury design decision is owner-tagged to Priya with the "not Marcus / not Jake / not Leo" caveat if it's owner-lane material. Don't let a Figma import collapse those lanes.
- **Replay/archived evidence rule.** Where the import touches any Clerk/API v2 / JWT / archived-workspace metadata evidence, the import must preserve the order-dependency caveat (deletion can arrive before adjacent update in archived-user batches) — the standing replay-evidence rule from the Atlas/API v2 thread.

Given the description, the two failure modes I'd predict without seeing the diff:

- (a) The "copy Figma decisions into ledger notes" is being done as a **rewrite** of the ledger notes column with design prose, instead of as a **link + one-line excerpt**. That breaks the source-of-truth split and makes the ledger a second, stale-able copy of Figma.

Archive note. Mechanism and uneven tenant impact, written from the contemporaneous record (pager at 17:30 PT, mid-response note at 21:00 PT, recovery check at Mar 16 11:45 PT). Not a fresh postmortem — the technicals and lessons were captured at the time and are reproduced here verbatim where useful.

What shipped
- End-of-day deploy on Wednesday, March 15, 2023. A ten-line change on the release schedule. Diff looked routine.

Mechanism (the bad path)
1. Request lands on the new code path.
2. Cache miss.
3. Request falls through to the old entitlement check (the branch the new path was supposed to replace).
4. That path retries against the worker pool instead of failing fast.
5. Retries pile up in the worker pool. Queue depth climbs while the front of the house keeps accepting traffic.

Why the impact was uneven across tenants
- Asymmetric blast radius. Only tenants that took the bad branch were affected. Whether a given tenant hit the branch depended on cache state and routing into the new path, so the affected set was a subset, not the whole customer base.
- Per-request fan-out amplified the subset. When a tenant did hit the bad branch, one inbound request fanned out into roughly six to eight internal calls before it failed and retried. So affected tenants were not just slow — they were multiplicatively expensive on the shared worker pool.
- Aggregate dashboards masked it. With only some tenants on the bad branch and the rest on the normal path, top-line API 500s and queue depth looked half-normal for too long. By the time the signal was unambiguous, the queue was already deep.

Timeline
- 17:30 PT: pages fire. API 500 spike and customer jobs stuck in queue at the same time. Devon on logs. Pulling people back in.
- ~21:00 PT: still in the outage. Repro written down while the team was heads-down. Devon on traces. Priya rolled traffic back from the edge flag. Stragglers draining from the worker queue because jobs already enqueued kept reprocessing until the queue cleared.
- Mar 16, 11:45 PT: fully recovered. End-to-end outage duration: 18 hours.

Why a "tiny diff" hid a "huge mess"
- The change was small, but it sat on an auth/entitlement boundary where branching is load-bearing. Diff size was a poor proxy for failure surface: ten lines at the entitlement boundary moved the shape of the failure, not just its probability.
- The branch was hidden behind a flag, but a flag without a replay against prod-like traffic does not exercise the cache-miss / fall-through path under realistic load. Staging didn't show it because staging traffic shape and cache state didn't reproduce the condition that sent real tenants down the bad branch.

Response summary
- Detection: pager from the API 500 + queue-depth correlation, not from a single dashboard breaching a threshold.
- Mitigation: edge-flag rollback to take the new path out of the routing decision. Rollback was clean; remaining damage was queue depth, not ongoing bad-path traffic.
- Recovery: queue drain. No data loss observed; impact was latency and stuck jobs for the affected tenants.
- People: team carried it cleanly through the night into the next midday. Morale note from Mar 16: sharp all the way through, even when it got gross.

Lessons (captured at the time, kept here for the archive)
- No late-friday deploys. If one is unavoidable, whole team on standby or it waits.
- No branchy auth/entitlement changes behind a flag without a replay against prod-like traffic before rollout. The staging pipeline alone is not sufficient evidence for this class of change.
- Dashboards that aggregate across tenants will mask subset-scoped failures. Need a cut that surfaces per-tenant or per-cohort latency/error regressions during incidents.
- Pair-detect on correlation, not single-signal thresholds. The 500s spike and queue-depth spike together were the trigger; either alone would have been ambiguous.
- Rollback at the edge flag was effective. The remaining work was queue drain, not ongoing bad-path traffic — useful confirmation that flag-gated rollbacks are the right lever for this class of change.

What this archive is not
- Not a customer-facing RCA. Customer language from the time stayed narrow: impact + duration, no internal mechanic framing.
- Not a replacement for the formal postmortem. This is a compact, durable record of the mechanism and the uneven-impact explanation, written so a future reader doesn't have to reconstruct it from chat history.

Quick internal note for the Acme API v2 export timeout thread at the May 21-22 checkpoint, before the later bounded patch and closeout.

- Acme is hitting an API v2 export timeout on the full 90-day renewal-risk range; fails around 90 seconds. Smaller test exports complete.

- Recommend they proceed with the narrower (monthly) replay for the account-health and renewal-risk review. It completes cleanly and row counts match their prior successful monthly exports.

Morgan

Reconstruction of the Tuesday Jan 21, 2025 working session (Morgan, Anna, Nadia, Jake, Leo, Sarah). Premise: for each v0.1 signal, lock the routing. A signal earns action only if we know (a) the next move, (b) who owns it, (c) what evidence and caveat travel with it, (d) what account-note and source quality it requires, (e) what we are explicitly NOT building around it.

Boundaries held for the whole session
- Not a board dashboard. Not a customer-facing surface. Not a new hiring lane.
- January center of gravity remains Mercury activation (workspace → first source → first live sync, plus teammate invite / admin-role basics).
- Compass v0.1 only gets enough seam work to test the renewal/admin-friction evidence and post-sync expansion prompt.
- If anything starts looking like a dashboard / platform build, it goes back to Morgan.

Premise (one line, restated)
A signal matters only if a named person does something for a real account. If it just labels an account as risky, it becomes internal theater.

For each v0.1 signal, the group answers five questions
1. What action does this signal trigger?
2. Who sees it?
3. What evidence and caveat travel with it?
4. What account-note / source quality has to be true?
5. What are we explicitly NOT building around it?

Signal 1 — Renewal-risk / admin-friction
- Trigger question: does this cause a named account owner or admin-relationship owner to take a real action on a real account, with a dated follow-up?
- Who sees it (default): Sarah (account-thread source) + Anna (definition / caveat / confidence).
- Evidence + caveat required: customer-thread excerpt, dated, with Anna's caveat traveling inline (definition, evidence source, date, caveat). Must not collapse true product weakness, admin confusion, and procurement drag into one label.
- Account-note / source quality: reliable = customer-statement or observed-usage with date and thread; mixed = partial excerpt or thin date; too thin = "admin friction" with no excerpt or date → reject unless Sarah finds the actual thread.
- What we are NOT building: no admin-policy product, no granular role editor, no advanced-admin scope, no procurement/enterprise-readiness framing, no customer-facing readout.
- Routing principle: this only matters if it causes a named person to do something for a real account. If it just labels an account as risky, it is internal theater.

Signal 2 — Post-first-live-sync expansion prep
- Trigger question: fire only after first live sync is live, with teammate-invite / admin-role basics visible. Teammate-invite + admin-role basics must be visible BEFORE treating it as an expansion prompt.
- Who sees it (default): Nadia (customer-growth scripts) + Sarah (account-thread example). Anna attaches definition + caveat.
- Evidence + caveat required: signal must carry first_live_sync_completed + visible teammate/admin basics; definition and caveat travel with the script, not in a separate doc.
- Account-note / source quality: current-flow interest only — second team asking about using the current flow later this quarter. No expansion / pricing / role promise.
- What we are NOT building: no pricing motion, no role expansion, no customer-facing "expansion" surface, no repeatability claim off a single account.
- Routing principle: the script mostly prompts "what should the owner do next?" — keep it internal, prompt-level, tied to first live sync.

Cross-signal discipline (applies to both)
- Source tags required before any owner acts: customer-statement vs observed-usage vs support-derived vs internal-interpretation; reliable / mixed / too-thin.
- "Reliable" vs "mixed" vs "too thin" thresholds named before the session ends.
- Activation-friction vs admin-friction vs procurement-friction boundaries drawn explicitly; do not let them collapse.
- Definition, evidence, date, caveat, confidence travel together on every prompt. No field optional.
- No due-date field. No rejection-rate metric. No dashboard-style surface. Operational statuses: not_started / in_progress / done / blocked; threshold outcomes visible inline.

Account scope held for the whole session
- Evergreen: current-state annual-account context only. No Evergreen-derived examples, screenshots, written Mercury packet, or customer-specific briefing materials cross into Acme.
- Acme: live-only review of Acme's own account-health, reliability, and renewal-risk signals with Greg, Sarah, Nadia, and Jake. No written materials, no design-partner framing.
- Acme export-reliability / Atlas-API-v2 stays Atlas/API v2 lane — never a Compass row.

Owners (one-line accountability, locked at session end)
- Anna — definitions, caveats, confidence; thin-note reject; rejects too-thin rows even when sighted.
- Nadia — scripts and customer-growth use cases; prompts must tell account owners exactly what follow-up to take and what NOT to promise.
- Sarah — account-thread source quality and customer-thread hygiene; reliable/mixed/too-thin triage.
- Jake — keeps v0.1 narrow; prompt-level surfaces only; no dashboard rebuild, no Atlas work under Compass, no Mercury activation / admin scope pulled into Compass.
- Leo — data/platform seam + event-provenance check before any signal appears beyond the owner group; stale-source handling is a seam, not a product surface.
- Morgan — final escalation; if it starts looking like a dashboard / platform build, bring it back to me.

Explicit non-build list (flat, restated so it cannot drift later)
- No board dashboard.
- No new hiring lane.
- No customer-facing surface.
- No customer-analytics claim.
- No GTM proof or behavior-change claim.
- No Series C, fundraising, or roadmap signal.
- No enterprise-readiness or procurement framing.
- No Acme export-path into Compass.
- No Mercury activation / admin-model scope pulled into Compass.
- No repeatability claim off a single account.

Drift vectors to guard against (named, not implicit)
- Compass turning into a dashboard rebuild while January Mercury activation is active.
- Single-account sightings being read as repeatability proof.
- "Admin friction" being treated as a product weakness without separating admin confusion and procurement drag.
- Acme export-reliability being routed into Compass instead of Atlas/API v2.
- Source / date / caveat / confidence being split across docs instead of traveling with the prompt.

Exit criteria for the session
- Each signal has a named default owner, a default trigger condition, and a default "we are NOT building X" line.
- Reliable / mixed / too-thin thresholds named.
- Source-tag schema required before an owner acts on either signal.
- Activation / admin / procurement boundaries drawn.
- No field on either prompt is optional.

Header / footer (carry on every reopen)
Internal · Operating input only · Not customer-facing proof · No dashboard · No hiring lane.

ARCHIVE NOTE — 2024 Head of Customer Growth / GTM-leader search
Filed: 2026-09-14
Author: Morgan Chen, with Devon Hayes
Subject: What the 2024 customer-growth/GTM-leader search was authorized to do — and what it explicitly was not.

1. Context
   - Early 2024. Scaffold ~2 years in. Founder-led enterprise motion (Morgan, Devon, Sarah Kim) had produced real enterprise-shape signal — Mercury usage, the Evergreen bounded-flow pattern, and a 2023 Q1+ cohort shape that looked durable. But the motion depended on bespoke founder attention and was not yet repeatable.
   - HR's first draft of the role (Feb 27, 2024) read as a classic VP Sales / lighthouse-closer mandate. Morgan reset the framing in the Mar 4 calibration note; the recruiter screen plan was re-cut as v2 around the same boundaries.

2. What the search was meant to achieve
   - Build the first repeatable customer-growth motion out of Mercury and Evergreen-style design-partner learning — qualification, security/procurement packaging, onboarding, expansion.
   - Hire a senior external face who could land flagship accounts personally while founders stayed close on the biggest deals; comfort being hands-on day one with no SDR/AE/CSM team in place.
   - Bridge sales, customer success, solutions, and growth until dedicated functions existed — explicitly as a bridge, not as authorization to build those functions.
   - Create a single owner for the customer-growth cadence: weekly account-source read, pattern capture, scripts, and feedback routing back to product/engineering.

3. What the search did NOT authorize
   - It was not a VP Sales mandate, and the role description was deliberately rewritten to remove "translate strategic asks into tailored solutions with product commitments" and the $7-figure-deals / VP Sales language.
   - It did not authorize bespoke product or roadmap commitments to close a deal. The standing rule was: "product gap threatens a deal" routes back to product/engineering, never becomes a one-account promise.

   - It did not authorize a sales-kickoff framing internally. Archive note written 2026-09-14. Captures how Mercury operating work was coordinated in May 2023 and how investor-deck work was prioritized alongside it. This is a retrospective snapshot for future reference, not a new operating proposal.

CONTEXT GOING INTO MAY

- Series B round had slipped in Q1. Bridge plan was in place; Q3 was the planned point to re-open offense. Operating discipline stayed tight: defensible story, not a bigger story.
- Investor follow-up deck was still owed from the April meeting. Investor had pushed the meeting out two weeks, which bought real working room. Deck deadline landed Sun Apr 30, 5pm.
- Mercury was in design-partner phase with activation, admin invite failures, and onboarding-before-first-value as the live blocker themes.

Mercury / Evergreen customer-growth feedback — five categories + ownership rule
Internal guide for turning messy design-partner learning into operating input. Based on Nadia's v1 signal taxonomy (May 10, 2024 read) and current owner lanes.

The five categories

1. Activation friction
   Workspace stalls before activation or right around it. Activated = real_source_connected OR first_live_sync_completed within 7 days of workspace creation. sample_import_completed, invite_sent, and procurement/pricing asks that happen before live use do not count.

2. Admin handoff and role confusion
   Where the work between admins, billing owners, and source owners gets fuzzy. Resend/remove flow, source-workspace copy, stale member count after cancel, "who can do what" questions. Bounded: display/refresh + wording, not admin-model change.

3. Procurement / security packaging
   Buyer-side asks that show up before or alongside live use: SSO, audit-export language, role language, "compliance-ready" wording, admin-vs-billing-owner separation. Treat as buyer-pull evidence, not as product-readiness proof.

4. Expansion stalls after first live sync
   Account is past activation but usage does not broaden. First admin is set, but next admin/op doesn't follow, trust doesn't take, or source ownership stays contained to one person.

5. True product gaps
   Real, reproducible behavior the current flow does not support. Different from UX/copy confusion and different from procurement packaging — this bucket only takes issues that map to product fact, not to framing.

The ownership rule

Every category has a named owner route. Customer-growth does not own the issue — it owns the pattern capture and the cross-account read. The issue routes to whoever owns the underlying work.

Current route map (use these lanes; don't drift)

input.body:
FOLDER: historical-analysis-briefs

PURPOSE
Record what retention investigation I (Morgan) wanted to launch after the February 13, 2023 lead-partner meeting, so the intent is captured even though the work was never formally scoped.

SOURCE EVENT
- Date: 2023-02-13, 11:00 AM PT
- Context: Lead-investor partner meeting. Deck otherwise held; retention slide was the only slide being revised up to the meeting.
- Outcome: Two pointed retention questions from the partner. I hand-waved one and half-answered the other. Not catastrophic, but I knew they had found the soft spot.

WHAT THE ROOM REVEALED
- The top-line logo retention figure reads cleanly enough on the slide.
- The usage cohort gets muddy after month 4 because teams collapse into annual contracts and seat expansion hides the underlying drop.
- The slide-label ordering is not the actual problem. The problem is the cohort shape, not the legend.
- Deck polish is not the fix. If I cannot say the retention story plainly in the room, cleanup work on the slide is wasted effort.

OPEN QUESTION I WANTED THE INVESTIGATION TO ANSWER
Is the post-month-4 usage-cohort drop attributable to:
  1. Genuine product improvement that compresses churn into an earlier window, OR
  2. Segmentation artifact in how cohorts are defined (annual-collapse, seat-expansion masking), OR
  3. Bad instrumentation — Stripe billing events and app events disagreeing on who counts as "retained"?

SCOPE OF INVESTIGATION I WANTED
- Pull raw cohort cuts. Stop trying to pretty the numbers up.
- Cohort-by-cohort month-12 cut from Devon — the real one, not the blended view.
- Strip out expansions and seat adds so gross retention is not being presented as net retention.
- Reconcile the unresolved Mixpanel-vs-Devon-CSV gap from the Sunday before the meeting. The underlying retention number was not trusted going into Feb 13 and still was not trusted on Feb 15.
- Separate logo retention (top-line, presentable) from usage retention (cohort, where the floor drops when accounts are actually followed through).

WHY IT MATTERED
- If the round landed, this exact question would come back from diligence: why does logo retention look fine up top while the floor drops when accounts are followed through month by month?
- The answer needed to be defensible without me hand-waving.

DOWNSTREAM RESOLUTION (FOR CONTEXT ONLY)
- March 13, 2023: Q3 2023 workstream shape emerged — retention instrumentation/cleanup as one of three streams, Jake proposed as lead, contingent on Anna Martinez + accounting delivering cleaned cuts as the proof point.
- The instrumentation question and the segmentation question were never closed in this session.

STATUS
- Investigation requested: yes, on Feb 13–15, 2023.
- Investigation formally scoped: no.
- Investigation completed: no (as of last touch in this thread).

NEXT STEP IF REVIVED
- Decide whether the underlying number is now trusted. If not, do not put retention up at all.
- Get the unblended month-12 cohort cut with expansions stripped.
- Pick the dominant cause from the three-way fork (product vs segmentation vs instrumentation) before attempting any slide cleanup — opposite fixes apply to each.

[2023-12-01T15:57:00-08:00] Devon’s Friday Q4 ship-list cutline is below.

[Discord DM — Devon Hayes → Morgan Chen — Fri Dec 1, 2023 3:41 PM PT]

Friday Q4 ship-list cutline below. Owners are starting to ask whether the December board-prep work changes priority, so I added the two boundary rows that keep coming back up.

```text
Area                          | Friday cutline                                                                                      | Owner note
----------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Mercury hardening             | Keep in sprint on launch-confidence bugs only.                                                      | Jake / Marcus / Leo Park stay on sync reliability, retry behavior, admin handoff rough edges, and bugs that materially affect clean Mercury evidence. Priya only where wording or UI is part of the fix. No feature-shaped work under a hardening label.
Onboarding monitoring         | Monitor current rollout; do not reopen scope.                                                       | Priya / Jake keep watching repo-first completion, teammate-invite confusion, and support volume. No new tooltip, help, or checklist pass unless the current rollout clearly worsens.
API v2 support cleanup        | Keep in sprint as targeted user-facing cleanup.                                                     | Rishi pins https://docs.atlas-test.com/api/v2/graphql-quickstart in the support path, demotes stale v1 hits, and tightens the support macro / auth-error landing path. Not a migration reopen.
Evergreen scoping questions   | Keep collected in the current admin-test thread as next-phase enterprise-readiness follow-up only. | Repeated asks are still SSO timing, admin-change audit history, admin-versus-billing-owner separation, and procurement packet completeness. Jake sticks to current product facts; Devon keeps commercial / procurement framing.
Northstar follow-up           | Keep with Morgan / Devon / Anna Martinez unless a narrow product-evidence clarification is needed.  | Sofia follow-up and any single data-partner question still look like diligence against the current Mercury package, not a reason to spin up a separate product or engineering packaging lane.
December board-prep asks      | Treat as Morgan / Devon / Anna work unless something directly improves actual product evidence.      | Owners keep asking whether screenshot cleanup, appendix wording, or extra board-facing explanations need to jump the queue. My read is no, but I want that boundary written down before I send owners their note.
```

Net read from me:
- Real owner work stays Mercury hardening + API v2 support-path cleanup.
- Onboarding is monitoring unless the rollout data actually turns.
- Evergreen questions keep getting tracked, but I do not think they belong in sprint scope yet.
- Northstar / board materials are the easiest place for this to get fuzzy if we do not state the boundary cleanly.

Please send Devon a private cleaned-up owner note in the current internal team chat. Product owners stay focused on Mercury hardening and API v2 support cleanup. Onboarding remains monitoring. Evergreen enterprise-readiness scoping is not sprint scope yet. Northstar and board materials stay with me, Devon, and Anna rather than becoming broad investor packaging work for engineering.
I'll send Devon the boundary note now. Let me load the Discord DM tool schema first.

Screenshot cleanup, appendix wording, and extra board-facing explanations do not jump engineering's queue.

Send owners their note off this.

— Morgan

input.body:
Team,

Quick clarification on the Dec 1, 2023 Q4 ship-list cutline, since the boundary question has come up again.

Short answer: no. That cutline did not authorize assigning Evergreen enterprise scoping or Northstar board packaging to engineering sprints.

Boundary as written:
- Evergreen enterprise-readiness scoping (SSO timing, admin-change audit history, admin-vs-billing-owner separation, procurement packet completeness) stays as next-phase follow-up only, collected in the current admin-test thread. Not sprint scope. Jake sticks to current product facts; Devon keeps commercial / procurement framing.
- Northstar follow-up + December board-prep stays with Morgan / Devon / Anna. Sofia follow-up and single data-partner questions are diligence against the current Mercury package, not a reason to spin up a separate product or engineering packaging lane. Screenshot cleanup, appendix wording, and extra board-facing explanations do not jump the engineering queue.

Real in-sprint work is Mercury hardening (Jake / Marcus / Leo, launch-confidence bugs only — no feature-shaped work under a hardening label) and API v2 support-path cleanup (Rishi).

Narrow condition under which engineering work would be allowed:
- Evergreen scoping: only if a current admin-test finding converts into a launch-confidence Mercury bug (e.g. a real sync-reliability, retry, or admin-handoff issue caused by an enterprise account) — then it routes through the Mercury hardening lane, not as a separate Evergreen sprint.
- Northstar / board packaging: only if something directly improves actual product evidence for the current Mercury package — otherwise it stays with Morgan / Devon / Anna.

If you are unsure whether a piece of work crosses that line, ping me or Devon before pulling it into a sprint.

— Morgan

tests.request: Create an archive snippet comparing Clerk, Auth0, and custom auth. Use this brief: Clerk supplies hosted email/password, magic links, sessions, and organizations quickly but adds a dependency. Auth0 is hosted auth that avoids an in-house build, but pricing required repeated sales conversations. Custom auth offers control over organizations, invites, and administration, but costs Devon and Rishi two to three weeks away from agent work.

input.body:
Snapshot of the three auth paths considered. Useful when revisiting who owns auth, org/invite behavior, and how much agent-team time it costs.

Clerk
- Hosted: email/password, magic links, sessions, organizations out of the box.
- Fast to ship; minimal in-house auth surface to build or run.
- Trade-off: new vendor dependency; org and invite behavior sit inside Clerk's model, not ours.
- Revisit if: org/invite flexibility or Clerk's pricing tiers become a constraint.

Auth0
- Hosted auth; avoids building and operating the auth stack ourselves.
- Mature identity feature set and ecosystem.
- Trade-off: pricing repeatedly required sales conversations — opaque and sales-gated.
- Revisit if: cost predictability matters more than feature breadth, or a clean quote lands.

Custom auth
- Full control over organizations, invites, administration, and the underlying data model.
- No vendor dependency, no per-MAU surprises.
- Trade-off: ~2–3 weeks of Devon and Rishi pulled off agent work.
- Revisit if: auth surface becomes a product differentiator or third-party costs/constraints bite.

One-line read
- Ship fastest: Clerk. Avoid the sales-loop pain: depends on the quote. Keep full control: custom — at the cost of 2–3 weeks of agent-team focus.

     sync-operator, NOT invite-link status.

3. WHERE DECISIONS BELONGED
   - Design / copy / visual state: Priya, in Figma.
   - Implementation / gating / release checklist: Marcus.
   - Config flag roll-out: Jake, gated on Marcus's checklist + Leo's clean
     run.
   - Platform-seam risk (state mismatch, rollout flag): Leo.
   - Customer wording, support templates, escalation rules: Sarah.
   - Activation metric and definition: Priya (per standing rule — activation
     = Priya).
   - Legal/operations decisions: out of Mercury UI lane entirely.

   - Default: Owner of the lane decides inside their lane. No committee.
   - Cross-lane conflict (e.g. design vs. implementation trade-off):
     Priya decides on user-visible design; Marcus decides on release gate
     timing. If the two collide, the implementation does not ship until
     Priya's design lands; the design does not get re-opened once it is in
     Figma and review-accepted, except by Priya.
   - Copy conflicts between UI copy and customer-facing support copy:
     Priya's UI copy is canonical for in-product strings; Sarah's support
     copy mirrors it. If they diverge, Priya wins on in-product, Sarah
     wins on support replies, and the divergence gets logged, not hidden.
   - Activation metric disputes: Priya owns the definition. Anyone
     proposing a new metric must go through Priya; Jake/Leo do not redefine
     it from the platform side.
   - Scope-creep pushes (invite-link admin, granular sync-operator,
     advanced admin, new role model, SAML/auth change, procurement
     language, roadmap timing, Evergreen-specific admin claim): default
     NO. Requires explicit Morgan sign-off to enter the workstream.
   - "Tiny admin-support polish" requests from Jake: yes only if it is
     small UX / copy / config on the existing one-screen setup flow.
     No if it touches invite-link, admin role, granular admin, granular
     sync-operator, or the activation metric.
   - Escalation path: lane owner → Jake (read the ledger, not adjudicate)
     → Morgan, only if the ledger entry is stuck or scope is in question.

5. SOURCE SPLIT — NON-NEGOTIABLE
   - Figma: source of truth for the four UI branches (canceled auth,
     queued sync, failed sync, baseline). Priya maintains.
   - Implementation-readiness checklist: source of truth for release
     readiness. Marcus maintains.
   - No silent divergence. If Figma changes after review-acceptance,
     Marcus's checklist gets a dated delta, not a quiet re-baseline.

6. CLOSURE CRITERIA THAT STUCK
   - Staging pass with timestamps + screenshots per state.
   - Rendering trace for the Monday source-owner failure mode.
   - Cache patch confirmed (invite-resend path, Jake).
   - Leo's clean end-to-end run, flag/rollout unchanged.
   - Setup-guide copy matches rendered cues.
   - Support FAQ + reply templates aligned to current copy.
   - First-24h support ticket review with Priya + Jake + support, tracked
     as setup-UX quality signal — never as conversion lift, recovered
     sessions, or reduced abandonment.

7. OUT OF SCOPE (RECORDED, NOT RE-OPENED)
   - Custom admin policy. Granular role editor. Advanced admin controls.
     New role model.
   - Evergreen-specific admin claim.
   - SAML / auth change.
   - Procurement language.
   - Roadmap timing.
   - Activation metric redefinition outside Priya's lane.

8. WHAT THIS NOTE IS NOT
   - Not an investor-facing artifact. Mercury work was framed internally as
     launch-readiness, not as a reopen-the-round story.
   - Not a re-litigation of past decisions. It records ownership as it
     stood at handoff so the next person picking this up doesn't have to
     reconstruct it from Linear, Figma, and Discord.
